communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the NY Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records created by or provided to the New York State Board of Elections between March 1, 2026, and the time this request is received:
1) All communications, letters, demands, instructions, and emails between United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (“USCIS”) agency officials, including but not limited to the USCIS’s Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate (“FDNS”), and state election officials regarding:
-- The implementation of Executive Order 14399 (“Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections”).
-- Development of a state citizenship list portal, including any records, including drafts, attachments, and implementing guidance, concerning the USCIS “Executive Order 14399 Implementation” memoranda directing the creation of infrastructure for state citizenship portals (June 8, 2026), https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.dcd.291053/gov.uscourts.dcd.291053.151.1.pdf. 
-- Plans to transfer personally identifiable data to create state citizenship lists, including receipts showing data transfer between relevant agencies.
-- Implementation of the “Unlawful Voter Initiative.” The “Unlawful Voter Initiative” refers to the initiative described in the “Disclosure Letter to Senator Padilla from Anonymous Whistleblower re: Department of Homeland Security and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services Direction to Identify ‘Unlawful Voters,’” (Sept 13, 2026), https://www.democrats.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/091326_-_senate_whistleblower_letter_dhs_uscis_combined_signedpdf.pdf. 
2) All memoranda of understanding (MOUs), data sharing agreements, or negotiations between state election officials and USCIS officials regarding granting federal agents access to personally identifiable data of state voters or the “Unlawful Voter Initiative.”
3) All log files, export or query counts, and metadata showing access of state voter data by USCIS personnel in searchable, machine-readable format, involving: time stamps, access metrics, confirmations of attestation statements (that the searcher is the voter or acting with the voter’s express authorization), search query parameters, pseudonymized user IDs, and system event codes. Remove personally identifiable information. 
4) Any internal complaints, alerts, incident investigations, audits, communications, reports, or notices regarding suspected violations of state election privacy laws relevant to the implementation of Executive Order 14399, the “Unlawful Voter Initiative,” and the creation of state citizenship lists. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I am willing to receive records on a rolling basis. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available in their native file format, to the extent possible. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 days.

Sincerely,
Michelle Du

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the NY Freedom of Information Law, Public Officers Law Art. 6, I hereby request the following records created by or provided to the New York State Police:
1) Between January 1, 2021, and the time this request is received: 
-- All internal and external communications, emails, proposals, memoranda of understanding (MOUs), user agreements, data sharing approvals, contracts, and data sharing agreements, between the New York State Police and Flock Safety (Flock Group, Inc.) or any local law enforcement agency, concerning use and access to the Flock network, the National Lookup tool, and Automated License Plate Reader (“ALPR”) systems. Include sharing settings of Flock databases.
2) Between January 1, 2024 and the time this request is received:
-- All log files or exports for queries executed by State Police personnel involving the search terms, queries, justifications, or codes: “ICE,” “Wanted by ICE,” “Immigration,” “Immigration (civil/administrative),” “DHS”, “CBP,” “Wanted by CBP,” or “Wanted by DHS.” Please provide information in searchable, machine-readable format, involving: time stamps, agency-level access metrics, search query parameters, and system event codes. Remove personally identifiable information. 
-- All internal and external communications, emails, and letters between the New York State Police and the Department of Homeland Security (“DHS”), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (“ICE”), or Customs and Border Protection (“CBP”), regarding cooperation, data access, or data sharing involving Flock Safety or ALPR systems.

I am willing to receive records on a rolling basis. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available in their native file format, to the extent possible. Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 days.

Sincerely,
Michelle Du

To Whom It May Concern:

I submit this Freedom of Information Act request for records concerning the implementation of Executive Order 14399 (“Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections”), on behalf of the University of Chicago Law School’s Data Ecology Research Initiative.

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I hereby request the following records created by or provided to the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (“USCIS”): 
1. Between March 1, 2026 and the time this request is received: 
a) Any records, including drafts, attachments, and implementing guidance, concerning the USCIS “Executive Order 14399 Implementation” memoranda directing the creation of infrastructure for state citizenship portals (June 8, 2026), https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.dcd.291053/gov.uscourts.dcd.291053.151.1.pdf. 
b) All emails, written communications, pre-decisional/deliberative and executed memoranda, data sharing agreements, data use agreements, contracts, plans, supplemental agreements, data transfer receipts, and policy directives sent or received between USCIS personnel (including, but not limited to, Joseph B. Edlow, Brian J. Broderick, and David M. Jennings) and any state government agency or state election authority personnel; Social Security Administration (“SSA”) personnel; Department of State (“DOS”); or United States Postal Service (“USPS”) personnel referencing one or more of the following topics: any steps to implement Executive Order 14399; the development of a state citizenship list portal and Login.gov; transfer of personally identifiable voter data to create state citizenship lists; and voter roll compilation, maintenance, and consolidation, including data segmentation activities and data integration methodologies.
c) Methods, pre-decisional/deliberative and executed memoranda, and instructions for USCIS personnel for obtaining voter data from states, commercial databases, public-facing portals for the purpose of creating citizenship lists.
d) Any system requirements, privacy considerations, technical blueprints, basic architecture plans (report generation, logging, and status tracking), and timeline and implementation roadmaps for the architecture of the state citizenship list portal, Login.gov, or the federated structure of the portal.

2. Between June 1, 2026 and the time this request is received:
a) Any records, including drafts, attachments, and implementing guidance (including re-staffing decisions), concerning the “Unlawful Voter Initiative,” referring to the initiative described in the “Disclosure Letter to Senator Padilla from Anonymous Whistleblower re: Department of Homeland Security and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services Direction to Identify ‘Unlawful Voters,’” (Sept 13, 2026), https://www.democrats.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/091326_-_senate_whistleblower_letter_dhs_uscis_combined_signedpdf.pdf. 
b) Training videos, memoranda, quotas, or materials related to the USCIS Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate (“FDNS”) implementation of the “Unlawful Voter Initiative” and instructions for USCIS personnel to investigate potential unlawful voters and enter “TECS” records. 
c) Legal guidance issued by the USCIS Office of Chief Counsel (“OCC”) directing FDNS personnel to research voter eligibility and internal documents by the OCC assessing the adherence of the “Unlawful Voter Initiative” to state privacy laws.
d) Any internal communications, agreements, data-matching protocols, final policy and technical directives, and contracts directing the creation of “source data” provided to USCIS personnel for the “Unlawful Voter Initiative.” 

Fee Category
I am requesting records on behalf of the University of Chicago Law School’s Data Ecology Research Initiative, an educational institution, as defined in FOIA guidelines. The request is made in furtherance of scholarly research and public understanding, not commercial use. I therefore am asking to be placed within the educational-research institution fee category, 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(ii)(II), and 6 C.F.R. § 5.11. If you require further verification of my institutional affiliation, please contact me immediately so I can provide my university credentials. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. 

I am willing to receive records on a rolling basis. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available in their native file format, to the extent possible. Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter.

Sincerely,
Michelle Du
University of Chicago Data Ecology Research Initiative

title: Chaffee Sheriff Office ALPR Audit History

communications.subject: Colorado Open Records Act Request: Chaffee Sheriff Office ALPR Audit History
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Per the Chaffee County Sheriff's Office Policy Manual, Policy 426 ALPR: 

426.3 ALPR OPERATION
d. No member of this office shall operate ALPR equipment or access ALPR data without first completing office-approved training.
& 
426.5 ACCOUNTABILITY AND SAFEGUARDS
e. ALPR system audits should be conducted on a regular basis.

• Please provide all documents considered to be part of the "office-approved training"

• Please provide a list of system audits that have been conducted since Dec 1st, 2024

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

William Beckett
